land.text: Ifat, ended in 1403; the Walashma dynasty returns

predecessors.note: Adal page: 'Adal Sultanate ... after the fall of the Sultanate of Ifat'; Sabr ad-Din III returned from Arabia in 1415.

land.text: the Ifat land held by Dawit I until 1415

predecessors.note: The Ethiopian Empire dossier carries the 1403-1415 gain and the 1415 loss.

land.text: the sultanate's last land; the capital moves to the oasis of Aussa in 1577

successors.note: Adal page: 'he then relocated the capital to the oasis of Aussa in 1577', and 'The Imamate of Aussa declined gradually ... and was destroyed by the neighboring Afar nomads'. The Emirate of Harar page lists the Imamate of Aussa as its predecessor.

land.text: the city of Harar and its plateau

successors.note: Emirate of Harar page: founded 1647 when the Harari 'refused to accept Imam Umardin Adam as their ruler'; Harar was under the Aussa imams (or Oromo pressure) between 1577 and 1647, which the pages do not describe.

capitals.name: Dakkar
capitals.note: Infobox 'Dakkar (1415-1520)'. The page gives no site or coordinates; the dot is a placeholder at Harar's coordinates.

capitals.name: Harar
capitals.note: Infobox 'Harar (1520-1577)'. Coordinates are Harar's in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Aussa (Awsa)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Aussa (1577)'; 'he then relocated the capital to the oasis of Aussa in 1577'. Coordinates are the researcher's (the gazetteer lacks Aussa).

rulers.name: Sabr ad-Din III
rulers.note: The page's sultan table. Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, who led the war of 1529-1543, is not in the table; Nur 'became the Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal' in 1550 though the table dates his reign from 1559.

rulers.name: Muhammad Nasir
rulers.note: Defeated and killed at the Battle of Webi River; the page gives no date for the battle, the Ethiopian Empire page says 1573.

keyframe_review.note: 149,495 km2 (bbox 40.3-45.1 E, 8.4-13.0 N): the old Ifat land, from the Harar plateau to the Zeila coast. The Adal page gives no area; it claims at Badlay's height 'the territory stretching from Cape Guardafui in Somalia to the port city of Suakin in Sudan' and, after Leo Africanus, 'all of the territory formerly ruled by the Ifat Sultanate' and the land east to Guardafui, which are reaches, not borders. Hadiya was an Adal tributary occupied by Zara Yaqob (table, undated). The shape stands as the core.

160,096 km2. The Adal page: Imam Ahmad 'finally decided to embark on a conquest of Abyssinia' in 1529; Dawaro and Shewa were occupied in 1531 and Bete Amhara and Lasta in 1533 (ledger), so the shape shows only the first strip of the conquest.

488,420 km2: the conquest at its height. The Adal page: 'Adal Sultanate occupied a territory stretching from Zeila to Massawa as well as the Abyssinian inlands'; the Ethiopian Empire page: 'by the mid 1530s most of Ethiopia was under Adalite occupation'. The Ethiopian-Adal War page has Tigray held 'roughly a year' from 1535.

correction.text: unchanged for 1540-1543; from 1544 the Harar core (new keyframe adal-sultanate_1544)

keyframe_review.note: The shape (487,589 km2) is right for 1540-1542. The Ethiopian-Adal War page: the Portuguese landed in February 1541; the Imam was beheaded on 21 February 1543 and his death 'forced an Adalite retreat from Ethiopia'; Abbas kept Bali, Fatagar and Dawaro until October 1544; 'Adal kept nothing of the highlands'. Cliopatria keeps the conquest to 1546; from 1543 the core only (ledger: February 1543 and October 1544).

correction.text: the Harar plateau and Zeila coast after the retreat

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1544-1546 (the Harar core before Cliopatria's Sultanate of Harar row begins in 1547). Sources as for 1540: after Wayna Daga (1543) and the death of Abbas (October 1544) Adal holds nothing of the highlands ('status quo ante bellum').

87,300 km2: Adal's remaining land, with Harar as the capital since 1520 (Adal page infobox) and Nur ibn Mujahid 'the Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal' from 1550. Wikidata gives this row the same item as the Adal Sultanate and the Wikipedia title is 'Adal Sultanate', so it is one state; the Emirate of Harar page dates a separate Emirate only from 1647.

76,402 km2, 12 percent smaller (the eastern edge goes from 45.1 to 44.7 E). No page opened dates a loss in 1564; the Oromo page has the Barentu Oromo invading Adal and Nur's army defeated at Hazalo, with Nur dying in 1567 amid epidemic and famine. Shape stands (cause unverified).

Same shape to 1578. The Adal page puts the sultanate's end and the move of the capital to Aussa in 1577; the Oromo page: 'the Oromo began their invasion of Harar region occupying as far as Hobat' and the capital move was 'due to the Oromo provocation in 1577'; the Emirate of Harar page: by 1577 the Oromo 'had destroyed more than a hundred villages and besieged the city'. The shape holds to 1577 here; Cliopatria's 1578 is one year late.

region.text: Adal, the Harar plateau and Zeila coast

ledger.note: 1415: Sabr ad-Din III returns from exile and refounds the Walashma sultanate as Adal. 'In 1415, Sabr ad-Din III, the eldest son of Sa'ad ad-Din II, would return to Adal from his exile in Arabia' (infobox 'Established: 1415'); Ethiopian Empire page: 'Walashma returned in 1415 and established the Adal Sultanate, centred on Harar'.
1415: the Ifat land leaves Ethiopian control. Same sentence as the founding; the Ethiopian Empire dossier carries the matching loss.
1520: the capital moves from Dakkar to Harar (infobox: Dakkar 1415-1520, Harar 1520-1577).

region.text: the land Cliopatria adds to Adal in 1529, the first ground of the war

ledger.note: March 1529: Imam Ahmad defeats the Ethiopians at Shimbra Kure. 'at Shimbra Kure in March 1529, where Ahmad's forces met the Christian king's army directly for the first time.' The page does not place the battle; the region is the strip Cliopatria adds to Adal's shape in 1529.

1531: Adal occupies Dawaro and Shewa. 'Dawaro and Shewa were occupied in 1531' (Adal page); the Ethiopian-Adal War page dates the victories 'that gave the followers of Imam Ahmad the upper hand' to 1531 (Antukyah 23 February, Ayfars 31 March).
1533: Adal occupies Bete Amhara and Lasta ('Bete Amhara and Lasta in 1533').
1535: Ahmad takes Aksum and Tigray ('marching into Tegray and seizing Aksum'); the hold lasted 'roughly a year'.
1536: Tigray is lost again (the year is the researcher's count from 'roughly a year' after 1535).

region.text: the highlands Adal evacuated, except Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya

ledger.note: 21 February 1543: the Imam is beheaded at Wayna Daga and Adal retreats from Ethiopia. 'the wounded Imam was beheaded on 21 February 1543 by an Ethiopian cavalry commander, Azmach Calite'; 'forced an Adalite retreat from Ethiopia'. The region is Cliopatria's 1540 shape outside the Harar core, less the south Abbas held until October 1544.
October 1544: Gelawdewos kills Abbas and takes back the south. 'in October 1544 ... Gelawdewos defeated and killed Abbas', recovering Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya.
October 1544: the war ends in an Ethiopian-Portuguese victory (infobox result; 'status quo ante bellum').

1550: Nur ibn Mujahid becomes Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal ('In 1550 Nur ibn Mujahid became the Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal'). Cliopatria names the state the Sultanate of Harar from 1547; the Wikipedia page, the colour and the dossier stay Adal's.

1577: Muhammad Gasa, who 'took the title of Imam' in April 1576, moves the capital to Aussa under Oromo pressure ('he then relocated the capital to the oasis of Aussa in 1577'; 'due to the Oromo provocation in 1577').

1577: the Adal Sultanate ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1577'); the Imamate of Aussa succeeds it. Harar, besieged by the Oromo, becomes independent only in 1647 as the Emirate of Harar. The page gives no day or month.

wars.name: Adal wars with Yeshaq I and Zara Yaqob
wars.outcome: No border change the pages name: Yeshaq I was killed fighting the Adalites in 1429 and Zara Yaqob defeated Sultan Badlay at Gomit in 1445.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian-Portuguese victory; status quo ante bellum. Adal held most of the highlands from the mid-1530s; the Imam died at Wayna Daga on 21 February 1543 and Abbas in October 1544.
wars.note: Ahmad promised to become a vassal of Suleiman I; 700 Ottoman soldiers and ten guns arrived in 1542.

wars.name: Nur ibn Mujahid's war and the Battle of Fatagar
wars.outcome: Adal's forces under Nur killed the Emperor Gelawdewos at the Battle of Fatagar in 1559; no border change the page names.
wars.note: The Ethiopian-Adal War page notes that Fatagar was lost permanently to the Oromo, without a date.

wars.name: Oromo invasion of Adal and Harar
wars.outcome: The Barentu Oromo invaded Adal; Nur's army was defeated at Hazalo, Nur died in 1567 amid epidemic and famine, the capital moved to Aussa in 1577 and Imam Muhammad Gasa was killed fighting the Oromo in 1583.
wars.note: The Hazalo battle is undated on the page. Reviewer af-01-b: end clamped from 1583 to 1577, Adal's end; the 1583 fighting belongs to the Imamate of Aussa.

wars.name: Sarsa Dengel's war with Adal
wars.outcome: Sarsa Dengel defeated Adal at the Battle of Webi River in 1573, after which Adal ended as a military power; Sultan Muhammad Nasir (1572-1576) was killed there.
wars.note: The Adal page gives no date for Webi; the Ethiopian Empire page says 1573.

certainty.note: Highland and lowland frontiers had no surveyed line; the conquered Ethiopian provinces 1531-1543 are only as precise as the occupation dates.

sources.title: Adal Sultanate
sources.note: Infobox (capitals, 1415-1577), the sultan table, the occupations of 1531 and 1533, Nur, the move to Aussa 1577.

sources.title: Ethiopian–Adal War
sources.note: The Ethiopian-Adal War 1529-1543: Shimbra Kure, Tigray 1535, Wayna Daga, October 1544.

sources.title: Oromo migrations
sources.note: The Oromo invasion of Adal and Harar; the capital move 'due to the Oromo provocation'.

sources.title: Emirate of Harar
sources.note: The Emirate of Harar (1647-1887): independence date, Imamate of Aussa as predecessor, the 1577 Oromo siege.

sources.title: Ethiopian Empire
sources.note: Walashma return 1415; Webi River 1573; Habesh Eyalet.

notes:
Two Cliopatria rows, one state. 'Adal Sultanate' (1415..1546) and 'Sultanate of Harar' (1547..1578) share Wikidata Q2365048 and the Wikipedia title 'Adal Sultanate'; the page says the sultanate had its capital at Harar from 1520 and calls Nur ibn Mujahid the 'Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal', so the Harar row is the shrunken Adal after the Gran war. One dossier under the earlier slug, with both Names in cliopatria_names; the sultanate-of-harar slug needs no dossier (colour: one family colour, rule 2).

Ends in 1577, not 1578 (Adal page infobox 'Disestablished: 1577'; the capital moves to Aussa). What follows: the Imamate of Aussa (Adal's successor, Afar plain; needs a dossier, slug imamate-of-aussa) and the Emirate of Harar (1647..1887, page: independent in 1647; needs a dossier, slug emirate-of-harar); the pages do not say who held Harar city between 1577 and 1647 beyond the Oromo siege.

Cliopatria problems: the 1540 shape keeps the conquest of Ethiopia to 1546 although the Imam died in 1543 and the south was lost in October 1544 (marked adjust; new keyframe adal-sultanate_1544 uses the Harar core). The 1564 shrink is undated. The page's claim of rule 'from Cape Guardafui to Suakin' is not drawn.

Disagreements: Sabr ad-Din II (lead) vs III (text); Sa'ad ad-Din II's death 1403 or 1410; Webi River undated on the Adal page, 1573 on the Ethiopian Empire page; Wayna Daga undated on the Adal page, 21 February 1543 on the war page; the Adal sultan table omits Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi. Gazetteer names needed: Dawaro, Bale, Fatagar, Hadiya, Bete Amhara (shared with the Ethiopian Empire dossier); Aussa and Dakkar have coordinates only (the dot for Dakkar is a reading, not a page).
Page budget: five pages (Adal Sultanate, Ethiopian-Adal War, Oromo migrations, Emirate of Harar, Ethiopian Empire) plus Ifat.
